headline: The same mutation
body: One receptor produced accelerated growth. The other produced severe growth retardation.
punch: Same mutation. Same hormone levels. Opposite outcome.

headline: Thyroid gets discussed
body: High, low, or normal. A number on a blood test that describes how much hormone is present.
punch: Which receptor reads it turns out to matter more.

headline: Put the mutation
body: Mice with a dominant-negative mutation in thyroid hormone receptor beta showed skeletal thyrotoxicosis — accelerated growth, advanced bone age, craniosynostosis.
punch: The skeleton behaved as if flooded with thyroid hormone.

headline: Put it
body: The identical mutation targeted to TR-alpha-1 produced the reverse: severe growth retardation, delayed ossification, delayed skull suture closure.

headline: And here's the part
body: The TR-alpha animals had normal circulating thyroid hormone levels. A blood test would have shown nothing wrong at all.

headline: The explanation
body: TR-beta dominates in the pituitary, so breaking it disrupts feedback and floods the system. TR-alpha dominates in bone, so breaking it deafens the tissue itself.
punch: One controls the thermostat. The other is the room.

headline: Which generalises
body: Every hormone in this topic is discussed as a circulating level. Receptor distribution decides which tissues can hear it, and that isn't measurable in blood.
punch: The level is half the story at most.

headline: And it's the same lesson
body: A man with normal testosterone never stopped growing because his estrogen receptor was broken. Different hormone, identical principle.
punch: Signal and receiver are separate failures.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
